question: Which observable dependence structures matter for diversification and risk-model adequacy, and do those observations improve held-out portfolio second-moment calibration?
data_frequency: US exchange-local trading-day adjusted prices; raw prices, corporate actions and reported volume retained separately
reserved_period: 2026 US equity price series not requested in the feasibility probe; decide its single confirmation use before fetching it
historical_holdout_limit: Major historical events are already known. An uninspected series is not a genuinely future or event-blind test.
portfolio: Fixed equal exposure to the nine sector ETFs; daily rebalanced idealized arithmetic-return basket, no execution or PnL utility claim
proposed_future_target: Mean of next five trading-day squared basket returns, using nonoverlapping five-day target blocks; not intraday realized variance or observed conditional variance
candidate_risk_controls: Diagonal covariance with matched per-asset variances
Fixed development-period correlation with rolling variances
baseline_note: The sklearn LedoitWolf scaled-identity implementation is not the constant-correlation target in Honey, I Shrunk the Sample Covariance Matrix. Final executable definitions must be frozen before evaluation-price download.
primary_future_score: QLIKE on positive portfolio second-moment forecasts; all controls and yearly results retained
uncertainty_plan: Paired resampling of nonoverlapping target blocks with additional dependence blocks, block-length sensitivity and yearly descriptive stability; exact block lengths/selection/family fixed in execution contract before evaluation download
network_interpretation: Correlation graph of observed ETF returns, not trader-interaction, ownership, causal or contagion network. Nine nodes cannot establish thermodynamic criticality or scale-free degree laws.

feasibility_probe.scope: Development dates only; schema and access check, not model selection or full data-quality acceptance
